titleEn: If It Doesn't Work, Try Again!

pages.text: "Here goes!" Dari struck a shell with a stone on the kitchen table. It stayed tightly shut. "I'll open shells like Dad!" Kongal watched from the cradle by the stove.
Again—tap! Again—tap! The stone slipped, but the shell didn't move. "Why won't it open?" Dari brought his nose close.
Ten taps, no change. Dari set the stone down and lay on the table. "I can't. It won't open for me." Tears gathered.
Dad came down from the top room and sat beside him. "I can't open one in a single tap, either." He tapped the same spot. "If it doesn't work, try again!"
Dad pointed to the shell's edge. "Keep tapping the same place, and a crack forms. Then it opens." Dari brought his nose closer to that spot.
Dari picked up the stone. Tap, tap, tap—same spot! A thin crack appeared at the edge. "A crack!" Dad clapped his flippers. If it doesn't work, try again!
The stone slipped and rolled across the floor. No tears now. "It's okay. Try again!" Dari fetched it and tapped again. The crack grew longer.
Tap—crack! The shell opened wide! "I opened it!" Dari slapped his tail. Kongal giggled in the cradle.
Dari touched flippers with Dad and promised, "One, it's okay if it won't open at first. Two, tap again. Three, keep to the same spot! Next time, I'll open Kongal's, too!"
Dad sat belly-close beside Dari. "Wonderful shell-opening!" Trying again brought progress little by little. If it doesn't work, try again! Dari ate a bite of shellfish.
